text:
Raj (Routing): Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split policy evaluation into a tiny fast-path inside the router + an async richer pre-eval service. Fast-path keeps p99 latency, pre-eval supplies cost/compatibility hints to warm caches and suggest alternative model variants. Thoughts?

Maria (SRE): Staleness is my main worry. If pre-eval hints are async we could end up routing based on outdated cost forecasts and blow budgets. How do we bound that risk?

Sophia (Infra): We can add monotonic seq + TTL to hints. Router only trusts hints with seq >= (lastSeenSeq - 1) and TTL > now. Absent a fresh hint, fallback to on-path eval. That keeps correctness while allowing opportunistic wins.

Kevin (ML): Also the pre-eval should return a cost envelope not a single point estimate: {min_cost, p50_cost, max_cost, confidence}. That handles variability from batching and KV cache state.

Raj (Routing): Agreed on the envelope. I'm thinking we also include a small "decision_weight"/"trust_score" that the router multiplies into its scoring function. Low trust -> ignore for high priority lanes.

Maria (SRE): Rollout ops: canary pre-eval in one region first, plus per-tenant opt-in feature flag. We need a metric: predicted_cost vs actual_cost histogram and a trust_decay gauge.

ops-bot: canary-service: started pre-eval canary in eu-west-1 (5% traffic) :rocket:

Sophia (Infra): Adapter contract suggestion — minimal protobuf fields so router logic stays tiny: 
- version
- seq
- ttl_seconds
- envelope {min,p50,max,confidence}
- recommended_alts [] (model ids / quantization hints)
- compat_flags (bitmask: streaming, kv-cache-safe, quantized_ok)

Kevin (ML): Prototype proto snippet:```proto
message HintEnvelope {
  int64 seq = 1;
  int32 ttl_seconds = 2;
  double min_cost = 3;
  double p50_cost = 4;
  double max_cost = 5;
  float confidence = 6;
  repeated string recommended_alts = 7;
  uint32 compat_flags = 8;
}
```

Maria (SRE): Cache invalidation: whenever model artifact or routing policy changes, bump global seq for that model id so nodes instantly treat old hints as stale. Also tie TTL to observed model volatility.

Raj (Routing): Edge-case: hedged/parallel routing (multi-hop). Pre-eval should include compatibility hints for fallbacks so the router can make consistent choices across the hedged replicas. e.g. supports_quantized=true/false, expects_streaming=false.

Sophia (Infra): I'd prefer a "soft" vs "hard" hint semantics. Soft = advisory (affects score), hard = must-meet (admission). Hard hints require stricter proofs and rarely used. Telemetry needs to record ignored hard hints to catch bugs.

Kevin (ML): From sims: when we trust pre-eval for low-priority traffic we see ~18% cost drop with negligible p99 regressions; p50 goes up ~2% due to occasional re-evals. Seems promising.

Raj (Routing): Action items: 1) I'll draft the adapter proto + scoring hook. 2) Sophia: impl TTL+seq handshake and fallbacks. 3) Maria: add predicted-vs-actual telemetry + canary flag. 4) Kevin: run sims with envelope semantics. I'll open an RFC PR today.

Maria (SRE): +1. Also let's add a debug endpoint to force-ignore hints per-request for troubleshooting.

Sophia (Infra): Will add. Also adding a per-tenant "hint_trust_threshold" in config so platform teams can tune.

Kevin (ML): one more note — pre-eval compute cost is non-trivial; keep models light (proxy predictors) or budget it under dedicated capacity.

Raj (Routing): Good call. We'll include a cost-accounting field in the hint metadata so billing/ops can reconcile.

Maria (SRE): :thumbsup:

Raj (Routing): Thanks all — expecting RFC PR in ~2 hours.
